reviews.name: Account number taken from second screen field when first field holds 99999999
reviews.statement: In the update-account program, when the account number entered (ACCNOI) equals 99999999, the account number passed on (COMM-ACCNO) is taken from a second account number field (ACCNO2I) instead. What 99999999 means to the business, and what happens otherwise, is not shown.

inputs.meaning: Account number entered by the user. The value 99999999 appears to act as a special marker rather than a real account (not confirmed).
inputs.comes_from: BNK1UAC:893 condition; the 'I' suffix suggests a screen map input field, but the trace does not name its source

inputs.meaning: A second account number field whose value is used in place of ACCNOI when the marker is present.
inputs.comes_from: BNK1UAC:894 (trace outcome 'from'); the 'I' suffix suggests a screen map input field, not confirmed by the trace

reviews.outcome: COMM-ACCNO is set from ACCNO2I (BNK1UAC:894). COMM-ACCNO looks like a communication-area field, so the chosen number likely decides which account is read or updated next. The trace lists no returned_to or reached_from entries, so where the value goes is not shown.

findings.what: The meaning of the value 99999999 is not explained in the cited code. It could be a placeholder that signals the real account number is in a second field, or it could be a test or default value. A person should confirm why this value switches the account number source.
Only the true branch is shown. The code that sets COMM-ACCNO when ACCNOI is not 99999999 is not cited, so the full account-selection logic cannot be confirmed from this candidate.

No validation of ACCNO2I appears before it is copied into COMM-ACCNO. If this number picks which account is updated, a wrong or empty value could target the wrong record. Any check would have to happen elsewhere and is not shown here.

This application looks like a retail banking account-maintenance program, not credit-card issuing. The pack's account concept covers open, change_limit and close, and none of these fits choosing an input field. For that reason no concept or policy was assigned.
findings.basis: BNK1UAC:893-894; program name BNK1UAC and paragraph UAD010

reviews.name: Account opening refused when the customer cannot be found
reviews.statement: A new account is not created unless the customer-inquiry program INQCUST confirms the customer record was found. If INQCUST reports no success, or the call to it fails, account creation stops with failure code '1' and the user is told 'The supplied customer number does not exist.'

inputs.meaning: Whether the customer record for the account was found. 'Y' means found; anything else means not found or the lookup failed.
inputs.comes_from: Returned by LINK to INQCUST (CREACC:327-330). Set to 'Y' when the customer read returns SQLCODE = 0 (INQCUST:353-355). Set to 'N' at INQCUST:206, INQCUST:441 (SQLCODE = 100 for an ordinary customer number) and INQCUST:731.

inputs.meaning: Whether the system call to the customer-inquiry program completed normally.
inputs.comes_from: CICS response to the LINK to INQCUST (CREACC:327-330), tested at CREACC:341.

reviews.outcome: CREACC sets COMM-SUCCESS = 'N' and COMM-FAIL-CODE = '1' (CREACC:344-345) and exits through GET-ME-OUT-OF-HERE (CREACC:347). The calling screen program BNK1CAC (link at BNK1CAC:775) sees SUBPGM-SUCCESS = 'N'. It marks the input invalid (BNK1CAC:845-847) and, for code '1', shows 'The supplied customer number does not exist.' (BNK1CAC:851-853). The 'The Account has been successfully created' message (BNK1CAC:929-930) is not shown.

findings.what: The same failure code '1' and the message 'The supplied customer number does not exist.' are given when the LINK to INQCUST itself fails. This is the EIBRESP not NORMAL condition. It is a technical error, not a missing customer, so the user may be wrongly told the customer does not exist.
findings.basis: CREACC:341-345 combines both conditions with OR. BNK1CAC:851-853 maps code '1' to the 'does not exist' message.

findings.what: INQCUST also sets INQCUST-INQ-SUCCESS to 'N' at lines 206 and 731. Line 206 looks like an initial default. The context of line 731 is not shown, and it may be an error or abend path such as a database failure. If so, a database error would also be reported to the user as 'customer does not exist'.
findings.basis: INQCUST:206 and INQCUST:731 are cited without surrounding code.

findings.what: INQCUST treats customer numbers 0000000000 and 9999999999 as special. Number 0000000000 retries with a random customer number (INQCUST:403-408). Number 9999999999 looks up the last customer number (INQCUST:417-423). If CREACC passes the user-entered number straight into INQCUST-CUSTNO, entering one of these values could make the lookup succeed for a different, real customer. The account would then be opened against that customer. How CREACC fills the INQCUST commarea is not shown.
findings.basis: INQCUST:403-423. INQCUST:434-441 shows that 'not found' is set only when the number is neither special value.

findings.what: The LINK stores its response in WS-CICS-RESP (CREACC:329), but the test reads EIBRESP (CREACC:341). These are the same unless another CICS command runs in lines 331-340, which are not shown. If one does, the test would check the wrong command's response.

This application looks like a general retail bank account-creation flow (customer number, sort code), not a credit-card issuer. No pack policy covers the check that a customer exists before an account is opened. CC-ACCT-1, ability to pay, is not what this code does, and no ability-to-pay check appears in the cited lines.

reviews.name: Account creation stops with failure code 9 when a system call fails after the customer check
reviews.statement: When creating an account, once the customer has been found, CREACC checks the response of the last system call stored in WS-CICS-RESP. If it is not normal, the request is marked failed (success flag 'N') with failure code '9' and the program exits without creating the account (CREACC:362-368).

inputs.meaning: Response code from a CICS system call made while creating the account; not normal means the call failed
inputs.comes_from: Set by RESP of the LINK to INQCUST (CREACC:327-330), the ENQ on the account-number counter NCS-ACC-NO-NAME (CREACC:437-442) or the DEQ on the same counter (CREACC:459-464). Which one holds the value at CREACC:362 is not shown.

inputs.meaning: Response of the most recent CICS command; must be normal to get past the customer check
inputs.comes_from: CICS runtime, tested at CREACC:341

inputs.meaning: Whether the customer the account is for was found; must be 'Y' to get past the customer check
inputs.comes_from: Returned by LINK to INQCUST (CREACC:327); set 'Y' when the customer row is read (INQCUST:353-355), 'N' at INQCUST:206, 441, 731

reviews.outcome: CREACC returns COMM-SUCCESS 'N' and COMM-FAIL-CODE '9' to BNK1CAC (BNK1CAC:775). BNK1CAC sees SUBPGM-SUCCESS = 'N' (BNK1CAC:845), clears the message, marks the input as not valid (BNK1CAC:846-847) and picks a message by fail code (BNK1CAC:849). Per the trace, the message shown is 'Account record creation failed, unable to count accounts.' (BNK1CAC:905-909). The success message and sort code display (BNK1CAC:928-932) are skipped.

findings.what: The check at CREACC:362 may never be true. The early exit at CREACC:341 already leaves when EIBRESP is not normal after the LINK to INQCUST (CREACC:327). Unless the lines between 348 and 361 (not shown) issue another CICS command that resets WS-CICS-RESP, such as the ENQ at CREACC:437, WS-CICS-RESP at line 362 still holds the LINK response, which already passed the test. A person should read CREACC:348-361 to see which call this check really guards.
findings.basis: CREACC:327-330, 341-347, 362; trace decided_by WS-CICS-RESP lists LINK 327, ENQ 437, DEQ 459

findings.what: The message the user gets for code '9' talks about being 'unable to count accounts'. That fits a failed lock (ENQ) on the account-number counter NCS-ACC-NO-NAME, not a failed customer lookup. The WHEN clause that ties code '9' to the text at BNK1CAC:905-909 is not among the lines shown, so the code-to-message link rests on the trace alone.

Line 365 sets COMM-SUCCESS in INQACCCU-COMMAREA, a work area for a different program. It is not part of what is returned to BNK1CAC (the caller passes SUBPGM-PARMS, BNK1CAC:777), so this value has no effect the caller can see.

The application looks like a retail bank (customers, sort codes, account creation), not a credit-card issuer. The 'account' concept is used only loosely. No pack policy applies to a technical failure during account creation.

reviews.name: Account opening stopped when the customer's existing accounts cannot be counted
reviews.statement: When opening a new account for a customer who has been found, CREACC asks INQACCCU for that customer's existing accounts. If that inquiry reports failure, the account is not created. CREACC returns success 'N' with fail code '9', and the screen shows 'Account record creation failed, unable to count accounts.'

inputs.meaning: Whether the lookup of the customer's existing accounts worked
inputs.comes_from: Returned by LINK INQACCCU at CREACC:1182. INQACCCU sets 'Y' at INQACCCU:448 and INQACCCU:486 (end of fetch). It sets 'N' at INQACCCU:196 (initial value) and INQACCCU:216 (customer not found).

inputs.meaning: Whether the customer exists; this is a precondition checked earlier
inputs.comes_from: Returned by LINK INQCUST at CREACC:327. INQCUST sets 'Y' at INQCUST:355 and 'N' at INQCUST:206, 441 and 731. Checked at CREACC:341-342.

inputs.meaning: Whether the CICS call to the account-count program itself worked; this is a precondition
inputs.comes_from: CICS RESP value (cics:LINK.RESP), checked at CREACC:362. The trace lists writers at CREACC:327, 437 and 459.

reviews.outcome: CREACC sets COMM-SUCCESS 'N' (CREACC:373) and COMM-FAIL-CODE '9' (CREACC:374) and leaves via GET-ME-OUT-OF-HERE (CREACC:376). BNK1CAC (LINK at BNK1CAC:775) sees SUBPGM-SUCCESS = 'N' at BNK1CAC:845, marks the data invalid (BNK1CAC:847) and shows 'Account record creation failed, unable to count accounts.' (BNK1CAC:905-909). No account is created, and the success message at BNK1CAC:929 is not shown.

findings.what: Fail code '9' is used for two different failures: the CICS LINK to the account-count program failing (CREACC:362-366) and that program reporting failure (CREACC:371-374). The user sees the same message for both, so support staff cannot tell them apart from the screen.
findings.basis: CREACC:366 and CREACC:374 both MOVE '9' TO COMM-FAIL-CODE; BNK1CAC:905-909.

findings.what: INQACCCU also returns 'N' when it decides the customer is not found (INQACCCU:215-216, including customer numbers 0 and 9999999999 at INQACCCU:835-844). CREACC has already checked that the customer exists (CREACC:341). If INQACCCU disagrees anyway, the user is told the system was 'unable to count accounts' and not that the customer does not exist, which is code '1' at BNK1CAC:851-852. The message may mislead in that case.

The count of existing accounts is probably used later to enforce a limit on accounts per customer. INQACCCU stops fetching at 20 (INQACCCU:463-464). This candidate does not show whether CREACC applies any such limit. If one exists, it is the business rule, and this check only guards it.

The trace lists WS-CICS-RESP writers at CREACC:327, 437 and 459 but not the INQACCCU LINK at CREACC:1182, which also sets RESP(WS-CICS-RESP). The check at CREACC:362 most likely tests the response from CREACC:1182. Someone should confirm which call's response it actually reads.

This application looks like a retail banking system (sort codes, customer accounts) and not a credit-card issuer. 'account/open' is only a loose fit. Nothing here checks ability to pay (CC-ACCT-1), so no pack policy is implemented or contradicted by this rule.
The cited source shows only WHEN '1' and WHEN '2' of the EVALUATE at BNK1CAC:849-855. The link from code '9' to the message at BNK1CAC:905-909 rests on the trace, not on a visible WHEN '9' line.

reviews.name: New account refused when the customer already has 10 or more accounts
reviews.statement: When a new account is requested, the customer's existing accounts are counted, and if the customer already holds more than 9 (10 or more), the account is not created. The request fails with code '8' and the screen shows 'Account record creation failed, (too many accounts).'

inputs.meaning: How many accounts the customer already holds. The check is NUMBER-OF-ACCOUNTS > 9.
inputs.comes_from: Returned by LINK to INQACCCU (CREACC:1182). INQACCCU resets it to zero (INQACCCU:461) and adds 1 for each account fetched (INQACCCU:583), stopping at 20 (INQACCCU:463-464). CREACC moves 20 into it before the call (CREACC:1176).

inputs.meaning: Whether the customer exists. The rule is only reached when the customer was found.
inputs.comes_from: Returned by LINK to INQCUST (CREACC:327). Set to 'Y' when the customer row is read (INQCUST:355) and to 'N' otherwise (INQCUST:206, 441, 731). Checked at CREACC:341-342.

inputs.meaning: Whether the account count was obtained. The rule is only reached when the count succeeded.
inputs.comes_from: Returned by INQACCCU (CREACC:1182). Set to 'Y' at INQACCCU:448/486 and 'N' at INQACCCU:196/216. Checked at CREACC:371.

inputs.meaning: Whether the call that counts accounts completed normally. A failure exits with code '9' before this rule.
inputs.comes_from: RESP of the LINK to INQACCCU (CREACC:1182-1184), checked at CREACC:362.

reviews.outcome: CREACC sets COMM-SUCCESS to 'N' (CREACC:382) and COMM-FAIL-CODE to '8' (CREACC:383), then exits (CREACC:385). BNK1CAC (caller, LINK at BNK1CAC:775) sees SUBPGM-SUCCESS = 'N' (BNK1CAC:845). It marks the data invalid (BNK1CAC:847) and, through the fail-code EVALUATE (BNK1CAC:849), shows 'Account record creation failed, (too many accounts).' (BNK1CAC:898-902). No account is created and the success message at BNK1CAC:929-930 is not shown.

findings.what: The limit of 9 existing accounts (so at most 10 per customer) is a literal in the code, not a parameter. A person should confirm this is the intended business limit.

The account count is taken before any lock is held. The only ENQ in CREACC is on the account-number counter (NCS-ACC-NO-NAME), not on the customer, and it comes after the check. Two requests for the same customer with 9 accounts running at the same time could both pass the check and leave the customer with 11 accounts.
findings.basis: Check at CREACC:380; ENQ at CREACC:437-442 on RESOURCE(NCS-ACC-NO-NAME).

findings.what: The cited excerpt does not show the WHEN '8' label above the 'too many accounts' message (BNK1CAC:898-902). The link from fail code '8' to that message rests on the reader's trace, not on a visible line.
findings.basis: BNK1CAC:849-855 shows only WHEN '1' and WHEN '2'; trace returned_to links SUBPGM-FAIL-CODE to BNK1CAC:898-902.

findings.what: This application looks like a retail bank (customers, sort codes, accounts), not a card issuer. 'account' is the closest concept. No Cards policy covers a per-customer account-count limit. CC-ACCT-1 (ability to pay before opening) is about a different check, and nothing in this trace shows an ability-to-pay check.
findings.basis: BNK1CAC:932 (SUBPGM-SORTCODE); CREACC:341-385 checks only customer existence and account count.

reviews.name: Account can only be opened for a recognised account type
reviews.statement: When a new account is requested, the requested account type passes the check only if it begins with one of ISA, MORTGAGE, SAVING, CURRENT or LOAN. In that case CREACC sets its success flag to 'Y' (CREACC:1310, CREACC:1315).

inputs.meaning: The type of account the user asked to open (ISA, MORTGAGE, SAVING, CURRENT or LOAN).
inputs.comes_from: The commarea that BNK1CAC passes when it links to CREACC (BNK1CAC:775-777, SUBPGM-PARMS), tested at CREACC:1310. The trace instead lists INQACCCU:595 / INQACCCU:466 (the ACCOUNT table fetch returned through the LINK at CREACC:1182). That source looks doubtful; see findings.

reviews.outcome: COMM-SUCCESS = 'Y' goes back to BNK1CAC as SUBPGM-SUCCESS (BNK1CAC:775). If the final value is not 'N', the screen shows 'The Account has been successfully created' and the new sort code (BNK1CAC:928-932). If it is 'N', the screen shows a message chosen by SUBPGM-FAIL-CODE, for example 'The supplied customer number does not exist.' for code '1' (BNK1CAC:845-853), and the data is marked invalid (BNK1CAC:847).

findings.what: The source the trace gives for the account type looks wrong. The test at CREACC:1310 reads COMM-ACC-TYPE IN DFHCOMMAREA, which is the request passed by BNK1CAC (BNK1CAC:775-777). The trace instead traces it to INQACCCU's per-account COMM-ACC-TYPE(NUMBER-OF-ACCOUNTS) (INQACCCU:595, INQACCCU:466), which sits in INQACCCU-COMMAREA (CREACC:1182-1183). The trace also shows no source for DFHCOMMAREA. Someone should confirm which structure line 1310 actually reads.
findings.basis: CREACC:1310 qualifies the field with 'IN DFHCOMMAREA'; CREACC:1182-1183 links INQACCCU with INQACCCU-COMMAREA; INQACCCU:595 moves the value into an array element; trace decided_by.DFHCOMMAREA is empty.

findings.what: The check compares only the leading characters ((1:3), (1:8), (1:6), (1:7), (1:4)). Any value that merely starts with an allowed word, such as 'ISA' followed by other characters or 'LOANXYZ', would also pass.
findings.basis: Condition at CREACC:1310 as given in the trace applies_when.

findings.what: The 'Y' set at CREACC:1315 marks only the account-type check in paragraph ATC010. The cited lines do not show whether later steps in CREACC can still set COMM-SUCCESS to 'N' before returning. BNK1CAC shows 'The Account has been successfully created' purely on the final flag, so this 'Y' alone does not prove the account was created.
findings.basis: CREACC:1315; BNK1CAC:845, BNK1CAC:928-930; the rest of CREACC after ATC010 is not shown.

findings.what: This application is a retail bank (ISA, mortgage, savings, current and loan accounts), not credit-card issuing. 'account' (open) is the nearest pack concept, but no card policy is implemented here. Nothing in the cited lines checks ability to pay before a LOAN or MORTGAGE account is opened, which a credit policy such as CC-ACCT-1 would expect.
findings.basis: Account types listed at CREACC:1310; no affordability fields among the cited lines.

reviews.name: Account opening refused for an unsupported account type
reviews.statement: A new account is created only if its requested account type starts with ISA, MORTGAGE, SAVING, CURRENT or LOAN. For any other type, account creation fails with success flag 'N' and fail code 'A', and the user is told the account type is unsupported (CREACC:1309-1318, BNK1CAC:912-916).

inputs.meaning: The type of account (product) requested for the new account: ISA, MORTGAGE, SAVING, CURRENT or LOAN.
inputs.comes_from: CREACC's own commarea, which the caller BNK1CAC passes as SUBPGM-PARMS on the LINK at BNK1CAC:775-781. How BNK1CAC fills the field is not shown. The trace instead credits the value to the LINK to INQACCCU (CREACC:1182) and from there to INQACCCU:595 and the DB2 fetch at INQACCCU:466-471. That source fills INQACCCU-COMMAREA, not DFHCOMMAREA, so the lineage needs checking (see findings).

reviews.outcome: CREACC returns COMM-SUCCESS = 'N' and COMM-FAIL-CODE = 'A' to BNK1CAC (CREACC:1317-1318, BNK1CAC:775). BNK1CAC sees SUBPGM-SUCCESS = 'N', clears the screen message and sets VALID-DATA-SW to 'N' (BNK1CAC:845-847). It then picks a message by fail code (BNK1CAC:849) and shows 'Account record creation failed, account type unsupported.' (BNK1CAC:912-916). No account is created. On success the user instead sees 'The Account has been successfully created' and the sort code (BNK1CAC:928-932).

findings.what: The trace's data lineage for COMM-ACC-TYPE looks wrong. The check reads COMM-ACC-TYPE IN DFHCOMMAREA, which is the request passed in by BNK1CAC. The trace's source for the value is the INQACCCU LINK, which uses INQACCCU-COMMAREA (CREACC:1182-1183), a different structure that holds the customer's existing accounts. The decided_by entry for DFHCOMMAREA is empty. Confirm that the checked value is the requested type from the caller, not a type read from the database.
findings.basis: CREACC:1309 condition names DFHCOMMAREA; CREACC:1182-1183 LINK uses COMMAREA(INQACCCU-COMMAREA); INQACCCU:595-596 moves into COMM-ACC-TYPE(NUMBER-OF-ACCOUNTS), an array entry in INQACCCU's commarea.

findings.what: The type check compares only the start of the field: the first 3 characters for 'ISA', 4 for 'LOAN', 6 for 'SAVING', 7 for 'CURRENT' and 8 for 'MORTGAGE'. A value such as 'ISAXYZ' or 'LOANS123' would pass as valid, so the check is looser than an exact list of allowed types.

The cited lines do not show which WHEN clause in BNK1CAC holds the 'account type unsupported' message. Only WHEN '1' (BNK1CAC:851) and WHEN '2' (BNK1CAC:855) are visible. The trace links lines 912-916 to this fail code, but a person should confirm it is WHEN 'A'.
The shown message has a doubled space: 'Account record creation failed, ' is joined to ' account type unsupported.', giving 'failed,  account'. This is cosmetic only.

This application looks like a retail bank (ISA, mortgage, saving, current and loan accounts), not a credit-card issuer. The pack concept 'account' (open) fits only loosely, and no Cards policy covers product-type validation.

reviews.name: Customer creation refused when the title is not an accepted value
reviews.statement: When a new customer is created, CRECUST checks the title supplied. If the title is not accepted, the customer record is not created: the program returns failure (success flag 'N') with fail code 'T' and stops (CRECUST:453-456). A blank title is accepted (CRECUST:446-447).

inputs.meaning: The customer's title (form of address) entered for the new customer
inputs.comes_from: Commarea passed by BNK1CCS on EXEC CICS LINK to CRECUST (BNK1CCS:997-999); checked in EVALUATE at CRECUST:415. Where BNK1CCS fills it is not shown in the trace.

inputs.meaning: Internal flag saying whether the title was accepted
inputs.comes_from: Cleared to ' ' at CRECUST:413, set to 'Y' at CRECUST:447 (blank title), set to 'N' at CRECUST:450 (condition not shown)

reviews.outcome: CRECUST returns COMM-SUCCESS = 'N' and COMM-FAIL-CODE = 'T' (CRECUST:454-455) and ends (CRECUST:456). BNK1CCS sees SUBPGM-SUCCESS = 'N' and shows 'Sorry but unable to create Customer record' (BNK1CCS:1069-1072). Fail code 'T' has no specific message, so the user is not told the title was the problem.

findings.what: Fail code 'T' (invalid title) has no matching message in the caller. BNK1CCS only gives specific messages for codes 'O', 'Y' and 'Z' (all about date of birth). The user sees only the generic 'Sorry but unable to create Customer record' and is not told the title is wrong.
A blank title is treated as valid, so a customer can be created with no title. Confirm this is intended.

The list of accepted titles (the WHEN branches between CRECUST:415 and 446) and the exact condition that sets 'N' at CRECUST:450 (probably WHEN OTHER) are not in the cited lines. The full set of accepted titles cannot be stated from the evidence given.

This is a retail-bank customer-creation check (CICS banking sample), not a credit-card issuing rule. No Cards pack concept or policy fits a title-format validation, so concept and policy are left empty.
findings.basis: CRECUST:453-456; BNK1CCS:1071-1092 messages refer to creating a 'Customer record'

reviews.name: Customer not created when no credit-check result comes back
reviews.statement: When a new customer is being created and the credit check ends with no result retrieved, the customer is not created. The credit score is set to 0, a review date is filled from WS-ORIG-DATE, and the request fails with code 'G' (CRECUST:473-483). The no-result cases are: the fetch ends unfinished with RESP2 52 and a count of 0 (CRECUST:767-777), or not found with RESP2 1 and a count of 0 (CRECUST:889-905). This check is reached only when the customer's title passed validation (CRECUST:453-456).

inputs.meaning: Whether the customer's title was accepted. 'N' makes the program exit earlier with fail code 'T', so this rule is never reached.
inputs.comes_from: Set by CRECUST from COMM-TITLE: blank at CRECUST:413, 'Y' at CRECUST:447, 'N' at CRECUST:450. Tested at CRECUST:453.

inputs.meaning: Flag meaning the credit check produced no usable result.
inputs.comes_from: Set 'Y' at CRECUST:777 and CRECUST:905, and 'N' at CRECUST:807, inside the fetch loop at CRECUST:741.

inputs.meaning: Runtime response codes from fetching the credit-check results. NOTFINISHED with 52, or NOTFND with 1, lead to the error flag.
inputs.comes_from: CICS runtime, tested at CRECUST:758, CRECUST:767-768 and CRECUST:889-890.

inputs.meaning: How many credit-check results were retrieved. The error flag is set only when this is 0.
inputs.comes_from: Tested at CRECUST:774 and CRECUST:896. Where it is counted is not shown in the trace.

reviews.outcome: CRECUST returns COMM-SUCCESS 'N', COMM-FAIL-CODE 'G' and COMM-CREDIT-SCORE 0 (CRECUST:474, 482-483), then exits (CRECUST:492). BNK1CCS shows 'Sorry but unable to create Customer record' (BNK1CCS:1069-1072). It has no specific message for code 'G'; only 'O', 'Y' and 'Z' are handled (BNK1CCS:1073-1083). The score of 0 is moved to the screen field CREDSCO (BNK1CCS:1109).

findings.what: Fail code 'G' has no matching message in the caller. The user gets only the generic 'Sorry but unable to create Customer record' and is not told the credit check failed.
findings.basis: CRECUST:483 sets 'G'; BNK1CCS:1073-1083 test only 'O', 'Y' and 'Z'.

findings.what: The credit score of 0 is moved to the screen field CREDSCO, as the trace shows, even though creation failed. A user may read this as a real score of 0. Whether line 1109 runs on the failure path depends on control flow the trace does not show.

A review date (COMM-CS-REVIEW-DATE) is built from WS-ORIG-DATE on this failure path, but no customer is created and the trace shows no caller use of it. It is unclear whether WS-ORIG-DATE is today's date.
findings.basis: CRECUST:476-479; the trace's returned_to has no use of the review date.

findings.what: The whole COMMAREA is written to the log on this path. It likely holds the customer's personal details (name, date of birth and so on), which may conflict with data-protection expectations such as CC-DATA-3. The COMMAREA layout is not in the trace.

A similar path at CRECUST:861-867 (INVREQ with RESP2 1) also sets the score to 0 and the review date. The trace does not show whether it also fails the creation or carries on, so the two failure cases may be handled inconsistently.

This is a credit-score lookup during bank customer creation, not a check of ability to pay before credit is extended on a card account. The application has sort codes and customer records, so no card-pack concept clearly fits and none was assigned. This rule refuses creation only when no score is obtained; it does not judge the score's value.

reviews.name: New customer refused when date of birth is invalid
reviews.statement: A new customer record is not created when the date of birth fails validation. This happens when the birth year is before 1601, when the date cannot be converted to a valid calendar date, when the customer would be over 150 years old, or when the birth date is after today. The same refusal also happens if the system cannot read today's date.

inputs.meaning: The customer's date of birth as entered on the create-customer screen. The year part is checked against 1601.
inputs.comes_from: Commarea passed by BNK1CCS in the EXEC CICS LINK at BNK1CCS:997-1003, tested at CRECUST:1560

inputs.meaning: The birth date converted to a day number. A failed conversion means the date is not a real calendar date.
inputs.comes_from: CEEDAYS conversion checked at CRECUST:1575-1581; compared at CRECUST:1606

findings.what: The agency programs do not assess the customer at all: each one returns a random number, ((999 - 1) * FUNCTION RANDOM) + 1. So the 'credit score' is an average of random values, not a real ability-to-pay check. This looks like a simulator or demo stub. A person should confirm whether real agency calls exist elsewhere in production.

This is customer creation in what looks like a banking application, not opening a credit-card account, so no pack concept or policy truly fits. If the score were used to grant credit, it would relate to CC-ACCT-1 (ability to pay). In this trace the score is only stored and displayed; no approve or decline decision uses it.

A score of 0 means 'no score'. If WS-NEW-CREDSCORE is a whole number, the agency formula gives values from 1 to 998, so 0 can be told apart from a real score and 999 is likely never produced. The picture of WS-NEW-CREDSCORE is not shown.
The average uses COMPUTE without ROUNDED, so any fraction is presumably dropped (truncated). The picture of WS-ACTUAL-CS-SCR is not shown, so this cannot be confirmed.

WS-CREDIT-CHECK-ERROR is set to 'Y' when no agency answered (CRECUST:905) and to 'N' otherwise (CRECUST:915). The trace does not show whether this flag stops customer creation or only marks the record. A score of 0 may be saved and shown as if it were a real score.

This candidate covers only the NOTFND path. It is unclear how WS-RETRIEVED-CNT can still be 0 here after all agency tasks have finished, for example if every agency reply failed to be read.

The review date is built from the WS-ORIG-DATE fields on the no-score path (CRECUST:900-903). On the success path the current date is read (CRECUST:927-928). How the review date differs between the two paths is not fully shown.

reviews.name: Customer creation rejects birth years before 1601
reviews.statement: When a new customer is created, a date of birth whose year is earlier than 1601 is rejected with fail code 'O'. The screen shows 'Sorry, customer is too old. Please check D.O.B.'

inputs.meaning: Year of the new customer's date of birth, as entered on the create-customer screen. It is a 4-digit number (CRECUST.cpy:18).
inputs.comes_from: BNK1CCS:995 moves screen field DOBYYI to SUBPGM-BIRTH-YEAR, which is passed in the COMMAREA by EXEC CICS LINK to CRECUST at BNK1CCS:997. DOBYYI is set to 0 at BNK1CCS:508.

reviews.outcome: CRECUST sets WS-DATE-OF-BIRTH-ERROR to 'Y' and COMM-FAIL-CODE to 'O' (CRECUST:1561-1562), then jumps to DOBC999 (CRECUST:1563). BNK1CCS receives the code as SUBPGM-FAIL-CODE and shows the user 'Sorry, customer is too old. Please check D.O.B.' (BNK1CCS:1073-1075).

findings.what: The message says the customer is 'too old', but the test is not an age limit. It only rejects birth years before 1601 (CRECUST:1560). Someone born in, say, 1700 passes this check, so the message overstates what the rule does. 1601 matches the earliest date that COBOL's date-integer functions accept, which suggests the limit protects later date arithmetic rather than setting a business age limit. That is an inference: the intent is not shown in the code.

BNK1CCS sets the birth-year screen field DOBYYI to 0 (BNK1CCS:508) and later passes it to CRECUST (BNK1CCS:995). If nothing overwrites it with what the user typed, a blank year reaches CRECUST as 0 and fails this check with the 'too old' message, not the 'D.O.B. is invalid' message (code 'Z', BNK1CCS:1081-1083). The cited lines do not show whether a screen RECEIVE happens between lines 508 and 995.

Whether a teller terminal using BNK1CRA ever reports 496, or whether 496 means another channel such as a web or API payment entry, has to be confirmed against the CICS CVDA list and the region setup. If BNK1CRA terminals never return 496, this refusal can never happen from BNK1CRA.

findings.what: The same MORTGAGE/LOAN + facility 496 test also blocks debits (DBCRFUN:330-335, fail code '4'). Together with this rule, mortgage and loan accounts can take neither credits nor debits from facility type 496, and both cases give the same code '4'.
A zero amount is treated as a credit here, because the debit path is only for COMM-AMT < 0. A zero request to a mortgage or loan account from facility 496 is also refused with code '4'.

On refusal the code jumps to UAD999 before COMM-AV-BAL and COMM-ACT-BAL are filled (DBCRFUN:375 vs 416-419). BNK1CRA moves SUBPGM-ACT-BAL and SUBPGM-AV-BAL to the screen (BNK1CRA:634-635). If those lines also run on the failure path, the screen shows whatever was already in the area, not the account's balances. It is not clear from the lines shown whether 634-635 run on failure.

The refused attempt appears to skip the transaction log. WRITE-TO-PROCTRAN is at DBCRFUN:441, after the jump at DBCRFUN:375. Nothing shown keeps the refused request with its reason code for review, which is what pack policy CC-POST-2 expects of rejected transactions. Whether UAD999 logs anything is not shown.

This application is a retail bank (current, mortgage and loan accounts with sort codes), not a credit-card issuer. The rule was mapped only to the generic 'transaction' concept, and no pack policy was claimed.

The business reason for blocking credits to mortgage and loan accounts from facility type 496 is not stated in the code shown. Possible reasons include repayments through a channel that is not allowed, or such accounts being serviced elsewhere. The owner should confirm the intent.

reviews.name: Teller debit/credit refused when the account balance update fails in the database
reviews.statement: When a teller debit or credit from the BNK1CRA screen has passed DBCRFUN's account read and its mortgage/loan and funds checks, but the database statement checked at DBCRFUN:425 returns a non-zero SQLCODE, DBCRFUN marks the request failed (COMM-SUCCESS 'N', COMM-FAIL-CODE '2'). It then runs its DB2 error check and exits (DBCRFUN:425-433). The teller is told the amount could not be applied due to an unexpected error.

review.proposal: The source cannot settle this. ODFACILTYPE is a CICS-supplied code for the kind of facility that started the task. BNK1CRA is a 3270 teller screen, so it likely returns a terminal-type value rather than 496. If so, the 496-based rejections at DBCRFUN:307-335 and 368-373 never fire from this caller, and every account read successfully reaches this update-failure check. Someone should confirm what 496 means and what BNK1CRA tasks actually return.

review.proposal: Cannot be settled from the lines given, because the SUBPGM-PARMS layout in BNK1CRA is not shown. BNK1CRA clearly expects to read success/failure, since it branches on SUBPGM-SUCCESS (BNK1CRA:581). If its commarea really is 92 bytes while PAYDBCR puts COMM-SUCCESS at offset 130, two things follow. DBCRFUN would write past the caller's area, and BNK1CRA would not see the 'N'. The teller could then get a wrong result message. Compare the BNK1CRA SUBPGM-PARMS definition with copybook PAYDBCR byte by byte, and check whether the reader's 92-byte size is right.

review.question: BNK1CRA reads SUBPGM-FAIL-CODE where DBCRFUN returns COMM-FAIL-CODE (offset 131): by position BNK1CRA has nothing (its area is 92 bytes)

findings.what: The SQL statement whose SQLCODE is tested at line 425 is not among the cited lines. The statement assumes it is the account balance update in paragraph UAD010, but this is not confirmed. Also, the code shown does not reveal whether a failure here rolls back related changes, such as a transaction record. CHECK-FOR-STORM-DRAIN-DB2 (DBCRFUN:432) is not shown, and the LINK uses SYNCONRETURN (BNK1CRA:516). Whether a failed posting leaves the balance unchanged, which is the intent of pack policy CC-POST-1, cannot be verified.

The precondition at DBCRFUN:307 refuses an overdrawing debit (WS-DIFFERENCE < 0) only when COMM-FACILTYPE = 496. For other facility types, a debit that takes the available balance below zero is not stopped and goes on to this update step. From the teller screen, overdrawing therefore appears to be allowed. Someone should confirm this is intended.

Fail code '2' collapses every non-zero SQLCODE into one generic 'unexpected error' message. The teller is given no reason detail, and nothing in the cited lines shows the SQLCODE being kept for review.

reviews.name: Customer delete stops when the customer lookup fails
reviews.statement: Before deleting a customer, DELCUS looks the customer number up through INQCUST. If the lookup fails, nothing is deleted and DELCUS returns success 'N' with INQCUST's fail code ('1' = not found, '9' or '0' = other failure). Otherwise processing continues and, at the end of the code path shown, DELCUS returns success 'Y' with a blank fail code.

inputs.meaning: Number of the customer the user asked to delete; it is passed to INQCUST as INQCUST-CUSTNO.
inputs.comes_from: Caller's commarea from BNK1DCS:1011, moved at DELCUS:297-298 (also used as the delete key at DELCUS:293-294)

inputs.meaning: Whether the customer lookup found the customer: 'Y' when found, 'N' when not.
inputs.comes_from: Returned by LINK INQCUST at DELCUS:303. Set 'Y' at INQCUST:355 (SQLCODE = 0). Set 'N' at INQCUST:206 (initial value), INQCUST:441 (not found) and INQCUST:731 (error path).

inputs.meaning: Why the lookup failed: '1' customer not found, '9' error path, '0' initial value.
inputs.comes_from: Returned by LINK INQCUST at DELCUS:303. Set at INQCUST:207 ('0'), INQCUST:442 ('1') and INQCUST:732 ('9').

reviews.outcome: If the lookup fails, DELCUS ends at DELCUS:315 and BNK1DCS (after its LINK at BNK1DCS:1011) shows a message and sets VALID-DATA-SW to 'N'. Fail code '1' shows 'Sorry but that Cust no was not found. Customer NOT deleted.' (BNK1DCS:1084-1091). Codes '0' and '9' match none of the code-specific checks at BNK1DCS:1084/1097/1109, so they reach the generic 'Sorry but an error occurred. Customer NOT deleted.' (BNK1DCS:1121-1127). If the lookup succeeds, DELCUS returns COMM-DEL-SUCCESS 'Y' and a blank fail code (DELCUS:347-348).

findings.what: The application is a retail banking system (customers, sort codes, customer delete), not credit-card issuing. Deleting a customer does not fit any Cards pack concept, and CC-ACCT-3 (no charges on a closed account) does not apply. Concept and policy are left empty.
findings.basis: DELCUS:289-298 (sort code and customer number key); BNK1DCS:1087-1126 messages refer to deleting a customer

findings.what: The log line says 'Customer not found' for every lookup failure, including fail codes '9' and '0', which are not not-found cases.

Lines 316-346 are not shown, so it is not visible whether the actual deletes succeed before success 'Y' is set. The trace only conditions 'Y' on the lookup succeeding. If later delete failures do not return early, a failed delete could be reported as successful.
findings.basis: Trace branch at DELCUS:347 with condition only NOT (INQCUST-INQ-SUCCESS = 'N'); DELCUS:347-350

findings.what: INQCUST treats customer numbers 0000000000 and 9999999999 specially. For 0 it retries with a random customer; for 9999999999 it reads the last customer. In those cases the lookup can succeed for a customer other than the one requested, while DELCUS keys the delete on the requested number. Whether a delete request can carry these values, and what DELCUS then deletes, is not shown.

The message checks in BNK1DCS appear as separate IF statements. The generic check at 1121 (success 'N' with no fail-code condition) would also be true for fail codes '1', '2' and '3'. If nothing between the IFs exits or uses ELSE, the specific message would be overwritten by 'Sorry but an error occurred.' The lines between the IFs are not shown.
The CICS RESP and RESP2 from the LINK to DELCUS are captured, but no use of them appears in the trace. A failed LINK would leave COMM-DEL-SUCCESS at whatever value it held before.

reviews.name: Account inquiry returns account details and always reports success
reviews.statement: When an account is looked up by sort code and account number, the account's details are returned to the caller: customer number, type, interest rate, opened date, overdraft limit, statement dates, and available and actual balances. The success flag is set to 'Y' whether or not an account was found; a blank account type, meaning not found, also gets 'Y'.

inputs.meaning: Type of the account found. Blank or low-values means no account matched the key.
inputs.comes_from: DB2 ACCOUNT.ACCOUNT_TYPE via SELECT (INQACC:843-848) or cursor FETCH (INQACC:431-436), moved to output at INQACC:542 / INQACC:949. Left blank by INITIALIZE OUTPUT-DATA when no row is found (INQACC:450-452).

inputs.meaning: Account number and bank sort code used as the lookup key.
inputs.comes_from: Caller's commarea INQACC-ACCNO (INQACC:263) and SORTCODE (INQACC:214, INQACC:265). Echoed back on not-found at INQACC:453-454.

inputs.meaning: Customer number, interest rate, opened date, overdraft limit, last and next statement dates, available and actual balance.
inputs.comes_from: DB2 ACCOUNT table (INQACC:843-849, INQACC:431-437), moved to output at INQACC:534-572. Copied to the commarea at INQACC:232-243.

reviews.outcome: BNK1DAC (link at BNK1DAC:554) shows the returned sort code, customer number, account number, type, rate, dates, overdraft and balances on the display screen (BNK1DAC:665-689). It shows 'Sorry, but that account number was not found.' only when account type is spaces, rate is 0 and INQACC-SUCCESS = 'N' (BNK1DAC:625-632). BNK1UAC (link at BNK1UAC:767) shows 'This account number could not be found' when COMM-ACC-TYPE is spaces (BNK1UAC:837-842; the full condition is not shown). Otherwise it fills the update screen from the commarea (BNK1UAC:852-873).

findings.what: Because of the finding above, BNK1DAC's 'Sorry, but that account number was not found.' message cannot be reached through this path. That message needs INQACC-SUCCESS = 'N', and INQACC sets 'Y' in both branches. A user who enters an unknown account would instead get the detail screen filled with blank or zero values. Whether another path in INQACC sets 'N' (for example an abend or DB2 error path) is not shown.

In the not-found branch INQACC does not copy ACCOUNT-TYPE or the interest rate into the commarea. INQACC-ACC-TYPE and INQACC-INT-RATE keep whatever the caller put there before the link. BNK1DAC's not-found test (BNK1DAC:625) therefore depends on the caller having cleared them.
findings.basis: INQACC:229-230 (only the success flag is set); INQACC:236-237 run only in the else branch.

findings.what: The trace links BNK1UAC:1024 (COMM-SUCCESS = 'N' → 'Update unsuccessful, try again later.') to the INQACC call at BNK1UAC:767. The messages at BNK1UAC:1028-1033 concern applying an update, so that check probably reads the result of a later update call, not this inquiry. Please confirm which call sets COMM-SUCCESS at that point.

This is a retail current and savings account inquiry (sort code, overdraft limit, available and actual balance), not a credit-card function. No Cards pack concept or policy fits, so concept and policy are left empty.
Line 231 (presumably ELSE) is not among the cited source lines. The two-branch structure is taken from the trace's branches.
findings.basis: Trace branches at INQACC:230 and INQACC:232; source shows lines 229, 230, 232 only.

reviews.name: Account inquiry fails when the customer is not found
reviews.statement: When the account inquiry for a customer cannot find that customer, it returns success 'N' with fail code '1' and stops (INQACCCU:215-218). A customer number of zero or 9999999999 always counts as not found, with the account count set to zero (INQACCCU:835-844); otherwise the customer counts as found when the customer inquiry reports success 'Y' (INQACCCU:855-856).

inputs.comes_from: Set to 'N' at INQACCCU:836 and INQACCCU:842, set to 'Y' at INQACCCU:856

inputs.meaning: The customer number the caller asked about
inputs.comes_from: Caller's commarea, passed in by the LINK at BNK1CCA:459, CREACC:1182 and DELCUS:409; tested at INQACCCU:835 and INQACCCU:841

inputs.meaning: Result of the customer lookup (the name suggests a customer inquiry call). 'Y' means the customer exists
inputs.comes_from: Tested at INQACCCU:855. The statement that fills it is not in the cited lines

(BNK1CCA:558-561). The trace shows no use of the result in CREACC (CREACC:1182) or DELCUS (DELCUS:409), and no caller reads the fail code.

Only INQACCCU:836, INQACCCU:842 and INQACCCU:856 assign it. If there is no ELSE branch and no initial value of 'N', a real customer number that is not on file may not take the not-found path at INQACCCU:215. Someone should check the code after INQACCCU:856 and the working-storage initial value.

Fail code '1' (customer not found) is never read by any caller. BNK1CCA shows the same generic 'Error accessing accounts' message for any failure, so the user is not told the customer does not exist.
findings.basis: INQACCCU:217; returned_to COMM-FAIL-CODE uses are empty for BNK1CCA:459, CREACC:1182 and DELCUS:409; BNK1CCA:558-561

findings.what: The trace shows no use of COMM-SUCCESS or COMM-FAIL-CODE after the LINK in CREACC (account creation) or DELCUS (customer deletion). If these programs truly ignore the result, they would go on as if the inquiry worked even when the customer was not found. They may instead rely on other fields, such as the account count.
findings.basis: returned_to uses are empty for CREACC:1182 and DELCUS:409

findings.what: This application is a retail banking customer/account system, not credit-card issuing. No Cards pack concept or policy fits a customer-not-found lookup result.
findings.basis: Program names INQACCCU, CREACC, DELCUS and BNK1CCA; message at BNK1CCA:560

reviews.name: Customer number zero treated as customer not found in account inquiry
reviews.statement: When the account-list inquiry (INQACCCU) is given a customer number of zero, it reports the customer as not found (CUSTOMER-FOUND = 'N') with zero accounts and skips the lookup (INQACCCU:835-838). Customer number 0 is never treated as a real customer.

inputs.meaning: The bank customer whose accounts are being listed; a 10-digit number (INQACCCU.cpy:8, PIC 9(10)).
inputs.comes_from: Passed in the commarea by callers: typed on the BNK1CCA screen as CUSTNOI (BNK1CCA:453, LINK at BNK1CCA:459); from CREACC's COMM-CUSTNO (CREACC:1177, LINK at CREACC:1182), which BNK1CAC fills from its screen field CUSTNOI (BNK1CAC:757, LINK at BNK1CAC:775); from DELCUS's COMM-CUSTNO (DELCUS:400, LINK at DELCUS:409).

reviews.outcome: INQACCCU returns CUSTOMER-FOUND = 'N' and NUMBER-OF-ACCOUNTS = 0 (INQACCCU:836-837) and exits through CC999 (INQACCCU:838). On the BNK1CCA screen the user sees 'Unable to find customer ' followed by the customer number, and the 10 account rows are blanked (BNK1CCA:529-540). BNK1CCA also checks for zero accounts and can show 'No accounts found for customer' (BNK1CCA:555-556). DELCUS only writes the account count to the log (DELCUS:414). The trace shows no use of either returned field in CREACC (CREACC:1182).

findings.what: The application is a retail bank system (customers, sort codes, accounts), not a credit-card issuer. No concept or policy in the Cards pack truly fits this input guard, so concept and policy are left empty.
findings.basis: DELCUS:441-447 selects CUSTOMER_SORTCODE and CUSTOMER_NUMBER; the BNK1CCA, BNK1CAC, CREACC and DELCUS screens and programs handle customers and accounts. Nothing in this trace touches cards, authorizations or interest.

findings.what: In BNK1CCA, it is unclear whether the zero-accounts check at line 555 also runs after the 'customer not found' branch. If it does, 'Unable to find customer' (BNK1CCA:531-533) would be overwritten by 'No accounts found for customer' (BNK1CCA:556), because this rule also sets NUMBER-OF-ACCOUNTS to zero (INQACCCU:837). The lines between 540 and 555 are not shown.

The zero-customer branch does not set COMM-SUCCESS (INQACCCU:835-838), but BNK1CCA tests COMM-SUCCESS = 'N' to show an access error (BNK1CCA:558-561). On this path, the value BNK1CCA sees depends on whatever was already in the commarea.

The trace shows that CREACC and DELCUS never test CUSTOMER-FOUND after calling INQACCCU. DELCUS only logs NUMBER-OF-ACCOUNTS. A customer number of zero would therefore not stop account creation or customer deletion through this flag; any guard would have to exist elsewhere in those programs.
findings.basis: Trace returned_to: CREACC:1182 has uses []; DELCUS:409 CUSTOMER-FOUND has uses [] and NUMBER-OF-ACCOUNTS is only displayed at DELCUS:414.

reviews.name: Customer number 9999999999 is treated as not found in the customer-accounts inquiry
reviews.statement: When the customer-accounts inquiry receives customer number 9999999999, it does not look anything up. It reports the customer as not found (CUSTOMER-FOUND = 'N') and returns zero accounts (INQACCCU:841-844). Customer number 0 is handled the same way just before this check (INQACCCU:835-838).

inputs.meaning: The 10-digit customer number whose accounts are being listed. 9999999999 is the highest value the field can hold (PIC 9(10), INQACCCU.cpy:8).
inputs.comes_from: Passed in the commarea by the callers. BNK1CCA:453 copies it from the screen field CUSTNOI. CREACC:1177 copies it from COMM-CUSTNO, which BNK1CAC:757 fills from its screen field CUSTNOI. DELCUS:400 copies it from COMM-CUSTNO, which DELCUS:559 may overwrite with the value read from db2 CUSTOMER.CUSTOMER_NUMBER (DELCUS:441).

reviews.outcome: Online account-list screen (BNK1CCA): CUSTOMER-FOUND = 'N' makes the screen show 'Unable to find customer 9999999999' and blank all 10 account rows (BNK1CCA:529-540). NUMBER-OF-ACCOUNTS = 0 can also set the message 'No accounts found for customer' (BNK1CCA:555-556). Delete customer (DELCUS): the program only logs the zero account count (DELCUS:414). Create account (CREACC): the trace shows no use of either returned value.

findings.what: The application is a retail banking customer/account system, not credit-card issuing. This rule is a customer-number guard on an account-list inquiry. No pack concept (account events are open, change_limit, close) or policy truly fits, so both are left empty.
findings.basis: INQACCCU:835-844; BNK1CCA:529-556; the callers are CREACC, DELCUS and BNK1CAC

findings.what: The code does not say why 9999999999 is reserved; no comment or caller explains it. It is the maximum PIC 9(10) value and may be a sentinel used elsewhere. If a real customer with this number could exist, that customer's accounts could never be listed, and the screen would wrongly say the customer cannot be found.

DELCUS does not check CUSTOMER-FOUND after calling INQACCCU and only logs NUMBER-OF-ACCOUNTS. For customer 9999999999 (or 0), it would see zero accounts as if the customer had none. Whether the deletion then goes ahead depends on code not shown.

findings.what: CREACC calls INQACCCU, but the trace records no use of the returned CUSTOMER-FOUND or NUMBER-OF-ACCOUNTS. The not-found result for 9999999999 may therefore have no effect on account creation. Someone should check whether CREACC reads these values in lines the reader did not trace.

In BNK1CCA, after the 'Unable to find customer' message is built (lines 529-533), a later check of NUMBER-OF-ACCOUNTS = ZERO sets MESSAGEO to 'No accounts found for customer' (line 555-556). The cited lines do not show whether the not-found branch exits first. If it does not, the not-found message would be overwritten and the user would see the wrong reason.

reviews.name: Account list returned only for a customer that exists
reviews.statement: Before listing a customer's accounts, INQACCCU looks the customer up through INQCUST. If the lookup does not report success, or the customer number is 0 or 9999999999, the customer is treated as not found and zero accounts are returned. Only a successful lookup marks the customer as found.

inputs.meaning: The 10-digit customer number whose accounts are requested
inputs.comes_from: Passed in the COMMAREA (INQACCCU.cpy:8). How the retry loops back (the GO TO RCD999 at INQCUST:408 and INQCUST:413, and the EXIT-VSAM-READ loop control) is not in the cited lines. The 1000-attempt limit is read from INQCUST:405 alone.

findings.basis: Trace returned_to BNK1DCS:866 has no uses; BNK1DCS:939-945

A person should check whether the condition is wrong or whether these lines are simply leftover code.

inputs.comes_from: Not traced. The reader lists no source for INQTRANL-LIMIT before the test at INQTRANL:218 (decided_by is empty). It may come from the caller's commarea or from a screen, but that is unconfirmed.

reviews.name: Account update refused when the account type is blank
reviews.statement: When staff update an account, the update is refused if the account type entered is blank or starts with a space. The account is not changed and the screen shows 'Update unsuccessful, try again later.'

reviews.name: Transfer refused when the amount is zero or negative
reviews.statement: The funds-transfer service (XFRFUN) refuses a transfer whose amount is zero or less. It sets success to 'N' and fail code '4', and the transfer screen tells the user 'Please supply an amount greater than zero.'

inputs.meaning: Amount of money to move from one account to the other. Signed, 10 whole digits and 2 decimals (XFRFUN.cpy:11).
inputs.comes_from: Passed in the COMMAREA by BNK1TFN as SUBPGM-AMT (BNK1TFN:496-502). SUBPGM-AMT is set from WS-AMOUNT-AS-FLOAT (BNK1TFN:494). That value is the screen amount field AMTI converted with NUMVAL (BNK1TFN:1006-1007, BNK1TFN:1190), after the amount text is unstrung at BNK1TFN:1042/1047.

reviews.outcome: XFRFUN sets COMM-SUCCESS to 'N' (XFRFUN:290) and COMM-FAIL-CODE to '4' (XFRFUN:291), then performs GET-ME-OUT-OF-HERE (XFRFUN:292). BNK1TFN sees SUBPGM-SUCCESS = 'N' (BNK1TFN:582) and marks the data invalid (BNK1TFN:584). It evaluates the fail code (BNK1TFN:586), shows 'Please supply an amount greater than zero.' (BNK1TFN:611-614) and goes to GCD999 (BNK1TFN:615). The user is not told the transfer was applied.

findings.what: This is a retail-bank funds transfer between accounts, not a credit-card transaction. 'transaction' (reject) is the closest pack concept, so no pack policy was assigned. CC-POST-2 asks that a rejected transaction be kept with a reason code for review. Here the code '4' is only returned to the screen (XFRFUN:291, BNK1TFN:586-615). The cited lines show no record of the rejected transfer being kept.

The screen program already rejects a zero or negative amount before calling XFRFUN: it tests WS-AMOUNT-AS-FLOAT <= 0 at BNK1TFN:1009 and a minus sign at BNK1TFN:1086-1090. From this caller, the XFRFUN check therefore acts mostly as a second, defensive check. Lines 1010-1014 are not shown, so it is not confirmed that the screen check stops the flow.

The XFRFUN check can still trigger when the screen check passes. WS-AMOUNT-AS-FLOAT is moved into COMM-AMT, which keeps only 2 decimals (PIC S9(10)V99). If the screen field allows more decimals, an amount below 0.01 (for example 0.001) passes the > 0 screen test but truncates to 0.00, and XFRFUN rejects it. The picture of WS-AMOUNT-AS-FLOAT is not shown.
The 'WHEN '4'' clause that leads to the message at BNK1TFN:611-614 is not among the cited lines. The link between fail code 4 and that message comes from the reader's trace, not from a visible line.
The cited lines do not show what GET-ME-OUT-OF-HERE does. They therefore do not confirm that no account is touched after the rejection, though the paragraph name suggests an immediate return.

The terminal then shows 'Transfer successfully applied.' (BNK1TFN:637-639).

Result of rolling back the unit of work after a failed step

reviews.outcome: COMM-SUCCESS = 'Y' is returned to BNK1TFN as SUBPGM-SUCCESS (BNK1TFN:496). BNK1TFN skips the failure handling at line 582 and the 'unable to determine success' message at lines 629-635. It shows 'Transfer successfully applied.' to the user (BNK1TFN:637-639).

findings.what: This application is a bank account funds-transfer function, not credit-card issuing. Concept and policy are left empty. The closest pack idea is CC-POST-1, which requires both balance updates to happen together or not at all. The rollbacks at XFRFUN:503, 679 and 826 suggest the same all-or-nothing intent for the two account updates, but the pack policy does not truly apply.

The sort-code half of the same-account check can never be false. Line 281 copies the same SORTCODE into both COMM-FSCODE and COMM-TSCODE, so line 316-317 compares only account numbers. Transfers can therefore only happen within this one sort code.

Every 'COMM-SUCCESS = 'Y'' branch of the line-378 condition also requires COMM-SUCCESS = 'N' at the same time, which is impossible. reviews.name: Successful transfer confirmed with the receiving account's new balances
reviews.statement: When a funds transfer has credited the receiving account (that account was read and then updated with no database error), XFRFUN marks the transfer as successful (COMM-SUCCESS = 'Y') and returns the receiving account's new available and actual balances. Each new balance is the stored balance plus the transfer amount. BNK1TFN then shows 'Transfer successfully applied.' and displays those two balances.

The receiving account's actual and available balances are shown at BNK1TFN:651-652. Changes are committed when XFRFUN returns, because the LINK uses SYNCONRETURN (BNK1TFN:501).

findings.what: This application is a retail bank funds transfer between deposit accounts, not credit-card issuing. No pack concept or policy truly fits, so both are left empty. The closest idea is CC-POST-1 (balances updated together, or neither updated on failure). XFRFUN does roll back on failure (XFRFUN:1111, 1204, 1403), but the pack's cycle totals do not exist here.

findings.what: The trace lists the debit lines XFRFUN:986/989 as sources of the balances returned at XFRFUN:1554-1555. On this path, though, the host row is reset at XFRFUN:1049 and re-read for the receiving account at XFRFUN:1057. The returned balances are therefore the receiving account's stored balance plus COMM-AMT, not the debited account's balance.

None of the cited lines check that the paying (FROM) account has enough available balance before the amount is subtracted at XFRFUN:986-990. The cited code could let an account go negative. Someone should confirm whether a funds or overdraft check exists elsewhere.

Each deadlock (SQLCODE -911 with SQLERRD(3) = 13172872) rolls back the work and adds 1 to a retry counter. While the counter is below 6, it rolls back (XFRFUN:1197-1208 and 1397-1407). The lines given do not show whether the transfer is actually re-driven after the rollback, or what the user sees once the retries run out.

The amount is converted with NUMVAL into WS-AMOUNT-AS-FLOAT (BNK1TFN:1006, 1190) and then stored in a field with two decimals (XFRFUN.cpy:11). The cited lines do not show that more than two decimal places are rejected. Extra decimals could be silently truncated.
